text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Lowen Ridge, according to a planning notice filed Tuesday with the City Registry and a statement from company chair Mara Venn. The project, first outlined in a transport briefing obtained by The Continental Record, calls for a 19-acre facility on the city’s eastern freight corridor, with space for 14 repair bays, a training wing and overnight stabling for up to 22 locomotives. Construction is expected to begin in March 2027, pending zoning approval. City transport commissioner Elias Brant said the depot would support “hundreds of regional service jobs” and reduce turnaround delays across the northern rail network. Kestrelline declined to disclose the final budget.
